commander: Major General William H. H. Morris, Jr.
current_activity: relieved west of Metz by the 95th Division and moves north for the XX Corps envelopment
notes: Event date: 8 November 1944 (Lorraine p375: the 10th Armored Division, intended for use with the 90th Division in the wide envelopment north of Metz, had been given a narrow front west of Metz in the first week of November; its final relief by the 95th Division was delayed until 8 November, by which time the main columns were already on their way north). Event definition: the division leaves its holding sector west of Metz for the XX Corps attack zone north of the city; this is its first Green Book appearance in the dataset and activates the unit. It is a movement date, not an attack date. Relationship: Third Army assigned; XX Corps (CMH table, from 23 October). Location: Division command post at Ottange from 9 November (atlas), the next day. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Ottange. Event support: moderate (single Green Book page for the date; the CMH table agrees on the corps and army). Location support: moderate (command post listed one day after the move).

commander: Major General William H. H. Morris, Jr.
current_activity: moves north to the Luxembourg-Bastogne area; CCB reaches Bastogne by the 18th
notes: Event date: 17 December 1944 (atlas: division command post at Luxembourg on 17 December; Ardennes p330: Bradley telephoned Patton on the night of 16 December that the 10th Armored Division would have to go north to help Middleton; p299: Team Cherry of CCB, 10th Armored, left Bastogne on the Longvilly road on the evening of 18 December). Event definition: the division leaves the Third Army's sector at Metz for the VIII Corps zone; the row dates the command post move to Luxembourg City, and CCB goes on to Bastogne. Relationship: Third Army assigned and XX Corps (CMH table, from 23 October; III Corps from 20 December). Location: Luxembourg City centroid, atlas date. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Luxembourg City. Event support: moderate (one Green Book page for the order; the move date comes from the atlas). Location support: moderate (one list).

commander: Major General William H. H. Morris, Jr.
current_activity: Task Force Richardson enters Trier before midnight and surprises the Germans
notes: Event date: 1 March 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 7 p. 133-134: on 1 March Combat Command A took Pellingen and Task Force Richardson, the 20th Armored Infantry Battalion, entered Trier before midnight, surprising the Germans; the task force is not a unit of the table, so the claim is the division's). Event definition: the division enters Trier in the XX Corps drive. Relationship: XX Corps unspecified_subordination (from 10 Feb 45 to 22 Mar 45, CMH table); Third Army assigned (from 10 Oct 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 17 Jan 45 to 22 Mar 45, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier assigned relation to 12th Army Group (CR0161) is closed at 16 January 1945 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. The earlier unspecified_subordination relation to VIII Corps (CR0165) is closed at 19 December 1944 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. Location: Trier city centre; the task force entered the city, no street is given. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Trier. Event support: moderate (single Green Book passage, two pages). Location support: moderate (named city; the entry point is not given).
